note.explanation: AI algorithms can be grouped by how easy it is to understand their decisions. Whitebox algorithms show an understandable decision-making process; blackbox algorithms make decisions that are not easily interpreted.
examples: A decision tree asks questions such as “Has feathers?” and follows the answers to identify an animal.
A neural network can process an image and identify it as a cat, even though its decision-making process may be difficult to interpret.
note.simple: Whitebox means you can follow how the AI reached its decision. Blackbox means that process is hard to understand.
note.checkQuestion: Which type of AI algorithm has a transparent and understandable decision-making process?
note.title: Explainable and Unexplainable AI Algorithms
steps: Identify whether the decision-making process is transparent and understandable.
If it is, classify the algorithm as explainable (whitebox).
If it is not easily interpreted, classify it as unexplainable (blackbox).
Use examples to support your answer: decision trees are whitebox; neural networks and deep learning models are blackbox examples.
note.answer: Explainable (whitebox) algorithms have a transparent and understandable decision-making process.

mcqs.stem: How does a decision tree help a computer make a decision?
rationales: Correct: a decision tree follows questions, with each answer leading to another question or a final answer.
Incorrect: hidden layers are associated with neural networks, not the defining feature of decision trees.
Incorrect: decision trees are not limited to learning from images.
Incorrect: a decision tree is an explainable method, not a set of unseen rules.

options: It finds a straight line that best fits data points

mcqs.stem: Which description best matches linear regression?
rationales: Correct: linear regression finds a line that best fits data points and can help show a relationship between two features.
Incorrect: a sequence of questions is the decision-tree description.
Incorrect: human-written if-then rules describe rule-based systems.
Incorrect: processing image pixels is not the definition of linear regression.

rationales: Correct: blackbox algorithms have decision-making processes that are not easily interpreted.
Incorrect: a flowchart is more closely associated with an explainable decision tree.
Incorrect: the number of questions is not the defining feature of a blackbox algorithm.

explain.title: AI algorithms
explain.body: Artificial Intelligence (AI) involves using algorithms and techniques to enable machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence. This section focuses on how different algorithms make decisions.

explain.title: Explainable (whitebox) algorithms
explain.body: Explainable or whitebox algorithms are those where the decision-making process is transparent and understandable. Decision trees follow questions to reach a result. Linear regression finds a line that best fits data points. Rule-based systems follow rules written by humans.

explain.title: Unexplainable (blackbox) algorithms
explain.body: Unexplainable or blackbox algorithms are those where the decision-making process is not easily interpretable. Neural networks and deep learning models are examples.

mistakes: Do not mix up the examples: decision trees are explainable; neural networks are given as blackbox examples.
Do not define the difference only by saying one model is more complex. The key difference is whether its decision-making process is understandable.
Do not describe linear regression as a sequence of questions; that is how a decision tree works.
When explaining a rule-based system, mention that humans write its if-then rules.
